intro.title: Build websocket server with rooms
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a WebSocket server that supports chat rooms, allowing multiple users to join separate groups and exchange messages in real-time. You will learn how to handle WebSocket connections, manage room-based message broadcasting, and track users across different rooms. The core programming concepts involve using event-driven programming with WebSocket events and managing shared state for rooms and clients. You'll work with the Node.js 'ws' library to create the server and use basic JavaScript objects to store room and client data. By the end, you'll have a functional server that can route messages only to users in the same room, demonstrating real-time, room-based communication.
intro.usecase: WebSocket servers with rooms are essential for building real-time collaborative applications where users need to be grouped by shared context. This pattern powers chat applications like Slack or Discord where users join specific channels, live multiplayer games where players are grouped by match instances, and collaborative editing tools like Google Docs where participants work on the same document. As a Node.js developer, you'll implement this to manage user subscriptions efficiently, broadcast messages to targeted groups, and maintain isolated communication channels within a single WebSocket connection.

objectives: Initialize a WebSocket server using the ws library in Node.js
Configure WebSocket connection event handlers for client connections
Implement room-based message broadcasting to specific client groups
Construct logic for clients to join and leave chat rooms dynamically
Integrate room management with WebSocket message routing
Manipulate client data structures to track room memberships
Apply error handling for WebSocket connection and message events

steps.title: Import WebSocket and HTTP modules
steps.instruction: Import the 'ws' WebSocket library and Node.js 'http' module using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use require('module-name') to import Node.js modules. You'll need both modules for creating a WebSocket server.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two require() statements that import the 'ws' and 'http' modules.
successCriteria: The 'ws' and 'http' modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported both the 'ws' and 'http' modules using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: import both the 'ws' WebSocket library and the 'http' module using require() statements.

steps.title: Create HTTP server instance
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server instance using the imported http module and store it in a variable named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the http.createServer() method without any arguments for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: An HTTP server instance is created and assigned to a variable named 'server'.
successCriteria: The code includes a variable declaration for 'server' that is assigned the result of http.createServer().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using http.createServer() and storing the result in a variable named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTTP server instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to use http.createServer() and assign it to a variable named 'server'.

steps.title: Initialize WebSocket server
steps.instruction: Create a new WebSocket server instance and attach it to the HTTP server you created in the previous step.
steps.hint: Use the WebSocket.Server constructor with the 'server' option set to your HTTP server instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a WebSocket server attached to an HTTP server
const wss = new WebSocket.Server({ server: httpServer });
steps.expectedOutcome: A WebSocket server instance is created and attached to the HTTP server, enabling WebSocket connections.
successCriteria: WebSocket server instance is created using new WebSocket.Server() with the server option set to the HTTP server instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're creating the WebSocket server with the correct constructor and attaching it to the HTTP server.
steps.feedbackWrong: The WebSocket server wasn't properly initialized. Check that you're using the WebSocket.Server constructor with the server option.

steps.title: Define rooms data structure
steps.instruction: Create an empty JavaScript object to store room data where keys will be room names and values will be arrays of client connections.
steps.hint: Define a variable using const and assign it an empty object {}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty object for data storage
const rooms = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: An empty object named 'rooms' is created to organize WebSocket clients by room names.
successCriteria: A variable named 'rooms' is declared and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created an empty object named 'rooms'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create an empty object named 'rooms' to store room data.

steps.title: Handle new WebSocket connections
steps.instruction: Add a 'connection' event listener to your WebSocket server instance to handle new client connections.
steps.hint: Use the 'on' method on your WebSocket server instance with the event name 'connection' and a callback function that receives the connected WebSocket client.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocket server will now detect when new clients connect and execute your callback function.
successCriteria: A 'connection' event listener is added to the WebSocket server with a callback function that receives the client connection.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an event listener, but make sure it's on the correct WebSocket server instance and uses the 'connection' event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The WebSocket server needs an event listener for new connections. Use the 'on' method with 'connection' as the event name.

steps.title: Create join room handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'joinRoom' that takes 'client' and 'roomName' as parameters and adds the client to the specified room in the 'rooms' object.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if the room exists in the rooms object, creates it if not, then pushes the client into that room's array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'joinRoom' is defined that properly adds WebSocket clients to rooms in the data structure.
successCriteria: The 'joinRoom' function is defined with two parameters, checks for room existence, initializes it if needed, and pushes the client into the room's array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function has both parameters, checks if the room exists, and properly adds the client to that room's array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The joinRoom function isn't defined correctly. It should take 'client' and 'roomName' parameters and update the 'rooms' object accordingly.

steps.title: Create leave room handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named leaveRoom that takes client and roomName as parameters and removes the client from the specified room in the rooms object.
steps.hint: Check if the room exists, then filter the client out of that room's clients array. If the room becomes empty, you can optionally delete it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A leaveRoom function that properly handles client removal from rooms.
successCriteria: The leaveRoom function is defined with client and roomName parameters and removes the client from the specified room in the rooms object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly removes the client from the room's clients array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The leaveRoom function isn't defined correctly. Check the parameters and removal logic.

steps.title: Create broadcast to room handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named broadcastToRoom that takes roomName, message, and sender parameters,
steps.hint: Inside the function, check if the room exists in the rooms object, then loop through its clients and send the message to each one that isn't the sender.
steps.expectedOutcome: A broadcastToRoom function is added that can send messages to all clients in a specific room while excluding the sender.
successCriteria: The broadcastToRoom function is defined with three parameters, checks if the room exists, iterates through the room's clients, and sends the message to each client except the sender.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function has all three parameters (roomName, message, sender), checks if the room exists, and sends the message to each client except the sender.
steps.feedbackWrong: The broadcastToRoom function isn't quite right. It should take three parameters, check if the room exists in the rooms object, then send the message to each client in that room except the sender.

steps.title: Handle client messages
steps.instruction: Add a 'message' event listener to each client connection inside the existing 'connection' event handler to process incoming data from clients.
steps.hint: Inside the 'connection' event handler, call ws.on('message', ...) to handle incoming messages. The message handler should parse the incoming data and decide what action to take.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocket server will now be able to receive and process messages from connected clients, enabling communication between clients and the server.
successCriteria: A 'message' event listener is added to each client connection inside the 'connection' event handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the message event listener is inside the 'connection' event handler and properly handles incoming data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The message event listener is missing or incorrectly placed. Remember to add ws.on('message', ...) inside the connection handler.

steps.title: Parse message commands
steps.instruction: Inside the 'message' event listener callback, parse incoming messages to identify commands like 'join', 'leave', and 'message' with room names.
steps.hint: Parse the message data string to extract the command and room name. You can use string methods like split() or JSON.parse() if the message is JSON formatted.
steps.expectedOutcome: The message event listener will parse incoming messages to extract commands and room names for further processing.
successCriteria: The 'message' event listener includes parsing logic that identifies commands like 'join', 'leave', and 'message' with room names.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your parsing logic can extract both the command and room name from the message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parsing logic is missing or incomplete. Try using string methods like split() to separate the command and room name.

steps.title: Wire handlers to message commands
steps.instruction: Inside the 'message' event listener, call the appropriate handler functions (joinRoom, leaveRoom, broadcastToRoom) based on the parsed message object.
steps.hint: Check the message.type property and call the corresponding handler with the appropriate arguments.
steps.expectedOutcome: The message listener now routes parsed messages to the correct room management handlers.
successCriteria: The 'message' event listener contains conditional logic that calls joinRoom, leaveRoom, or broadcastToRoom based on message.type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling all three handler functions (joinRoom, leaveRoom, broadcastToRoom) based on the message type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The message listener doesn't properly route commands to handlers. Check the analogous example for the correct conditional structure.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.instruction: Make the HTTP server listen on port 8080 to start accepting WebSocket connections.
steps.hint: Use the server.listen() method with the port number and an optional callback function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be ready to accept WebSocket connections on port 8080.
successCriteria: The server.listen() method is called with port 8080 and an optional callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure you're using port 8080 and optionally include a callback to log a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. Use server.listen() with port 8080 to begin accepting connections.
